title: The Twelfth Arithmetic

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Twelve times the figure went over the basket and twelve times it went up the road in a locked box. The pot kept its crack and the year kept its cold, and the hand that wrote went home believing well of itself.
epigraph.attribution: A Low Kiln saying, told at the last market of the year

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of three hundred and eighty-seven to three hundred and eighty-nine days, six months and two hundred and seven to two hundred and nine days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. As in chapters 25 through 111 the old life is carried by the surgeon's register alone: no present-tense break, no tagged memory, no departure from the boy's eyes, and the carried fire's payer stays unnamed. Each morning the register takes the body in its old order — one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool; the empty place beside it holding the fold of wool Sella put there on the fifteenth, found where put and not made again, still a finding and not a placing; the thread of drool frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — while the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrels without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. The chapter lives the year's last three days: two ordinary tending days under the Vail roof and the year's third and last Account-day and market on Stone 30, where the twelfth arithmetic goes up behind one unsigned figure. Twelve are twelve and not one account, the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space and no doctrine comes out of twelve. The keeping at the fold stays a finding, the four directions stand where put and do not repeat, the six hearings keep the seventh place empty, the widow's mark is untouched, and the year ends without a boundary drawn, neither of the district's two habits of naming its months set right or left. The Five stand beyond the close and are not brought in.
places: the reading block under the moot-post
the flat stone by the well

scenes.title: Two Mornings Off
scenes.synopsis: First entry, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first \daymark{387}{Stone 28, Eighthday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours opening the second-to-last day of the year under the Vail kiln-house roof in Low Kiln, Sill, Grath, hand laid flat on answer 348 and count exact at 386 carried in from Chapter 111. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail; Garl Vail in objects only (the salt-stiff coat with its left-shoulder crease on the peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the clean dark line at the Vail corner with its finer grey called the thaw thickened in the dry cold with the faint sour tang of Ash, the twice-mended pot's hairline, the unforged collector sentence at the kindling, the uncalled tile debt). No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, Tarn, Jorra, collector, runner, market, Cross or bell on this morning; no ownerless voice over the boards — the Ash 5 joining and the Ash 17, Ash 23 and Stone 23 directions stand where put and do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). New day, new date, no recap: nothing from Stone 25, 26 or 27 crosses as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Dramatic purpose: the count goes on and the year's last reading stands two mornings off without being brought into a day that has not earned it. The surgeon takes the body in its old order — the leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the empty place beside it holding the fold put there on the fifteenth and found where put and not made again, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and knows a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the rewarming he would choose and cannot ask for, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from the outside and slowly, never hurried, never rubbed, while the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrels without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086). Sella goes to the hearth before the basket, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says the house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glances once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with her hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crosses the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person, turns the dressed grain under wool with no figure and no handful, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, carries him down the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate with the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire and never to the basket, and goes wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T058/T079/T100, T077, T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). The keeping is found where put and stays a finding, not a placing, not a habit, way, sign, hearing, mending, cause or rule, with no second fold, third crust, name, gift, payment or payer. Three counts in three places do not rise into one; six hearings stand beside and never among with the seventh place empty and the Drawing's flat knock outside; the heard bell keeps its square beside the told; eleven arithmetics stand behind one unsigned figure with no twelfth brought early. Answer **349** filed on the towel in the small hours: exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across none of the kept things.

scenes.title: The Seventh Year at Its End
scenes.synopsis: Second entry, no new dated heading: the afternoon of Stone 28 through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day with answer 350. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge and damper; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons only: a Cold Acre hare-carrier shifting a hare across his shoulders, a cracked-jar man in a rope sling, a woman with a basket of kindling, two fence-menders arguing the thaw. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, collector, green-mouthed woman or foundling; no market, Cross or bell; no ownerless voice — the four directions stand where put and do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). Dramatic purpose: the loan stays uncalled at the very end of a seventh year and the equality under the roof holds without a word while the year runs toward its last reading. Out in the Clay Yard the afternoon stands in the dry cold and the yard goes around its seven places with a look and a wide step and no number, once and not twice (T009/T013/T092). The clean dark line at the Vail corner and its finer grey called the thaw stay unswept with the faint sour tang of Ash; the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody; the round ring where the shallow pan once stood keeps no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word; the gone frost off the well's north lip, the skin on the trough and the silt-clouded plate on its flat stone stay weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair; out on the worked strips the field keeps its empty place (T083/T085 held). The hare-carrier answers the price with the weather which carried the snow and can carry the price, the cracked-jar man is sent to a pot that says nothing, and to the woman with kindling asking what the seventh year will want and the two fence-menders wanting the thaw early and late Tarn says Yes, house to each and keeps the late because it puts off the paying, agreeing so thoroughly that no argument finds a foot (T077). At the kindling six pieces lie in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt; the small knife lies at the very edge of its sill, his hand passes over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, and he tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, cutting, counting and spending nothing. The Ash 14 held breath and the Bone 26 thumb's resting are found where put and not made again, beside the five held objects and the pot-crack resting with a finger between every pair; he brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year now at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled, and does not look along the road — a term ending is not a payment, a forgiveness or a freedom, and the fear of being entered again for vagrancy stays his (T036/T076/T006). Jorra comes through the finger's-width door with meal-fine grey slate dust white in a fist-crease, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; three or more men unnamed went low into the back room before first grey and get no name from him and no word that the room was cold; dusty forearms are parted from clean as clot from vessel, the wheel and a pot are spoken to before any person, the full note known three turns ahead is withheld from any High Kiln master who would call it early, and his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence and out without a second holding of Ash 26 — one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word covering both mercies (T062/T035/T031). He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn while the burned slate stands at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with no witness and the well-saying at four shapings. At the going of the light Sella carries him up the nineteen steps and never into the Debt Loft, sets him on his bed, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and adds no second fold, renews the hearth grammar and leaves the twice-mended pot, dressed grain, unread charcoal and untouched widow's mark as found. In the small hours the file comes out on the towel with every gap left gap; answer **350** is filed exact, complete and worth nothing, and the twelfth arithmetic still gathers two mornings ahead unbrought.

scenes.title: The Count in the Wood
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and the second dated \daymark{388}{Stone 29, Ninthday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours opening the last ordinary day of the year, hand laid flat on answer 350 and count exact at 387 carried in, moving into the morning. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Ilva once at the yard well; Garl Vail in objects. No Berr, Hessa, Tarn, Jorra, collector, runner, market, Cross or bell; no ownerless voice — the Ash 5 joining and the Ash 17, Ash 23 and Stone 23 directions stand where put and do not repeat (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). New day, new date, no recap: the keeping found where put yesterday was a finding and not a habit, and eleven arithmetics stand behind one unsigned figure without a doctrine. Dramatic purpose: a count kept in wood stays in wood, set against the figure that will be read over the basket tomorrow, and the boy refuses to turn a ninth hand's record into a figure. The surgeon takes the body in its old order — leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its corner a hair off the wool; cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it; a face composed by cold is not composure and pink returning is the surface still cold over the core; the afterdrop waits past a warming nobody here will perform — while the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrels without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086). The keeping is found where put and not made again, still a finding and not a placing; a habit wants a hand that placed twice and a way a third, and both want a payer where none stands. At the yard well Ilva draws with the pail against her knee, the rope stiff in the Stone cold giving its small dry rasp, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and the finer grey rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb she does not scrub out; people notice the pail first and the sleeve not at all. To the woman waiting her turn who asks what Stone's firings have taken, her hand goes toward her sleeve before her eyes go to the asker and her mouth opens after both, the half-beat lying in the gap where a lesser observer would put an intention. The short strip of notched birch bark lies in the fold where it always lies, pale where a thumb has rubbed the notches and dark in the uncut grain between; it is not taken out, read, copied, counted or joined to the open slate a pace away on the stone lip, to the charcoal beneath the loaf shelf, to the cord or the knot-string, and no figure comes off the wood. She answers the question put and not the one behind it: Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account, puts the flat of her hand once more on the sleeve and goes back to the pail, and nobody turns twice. The boy takes the order of reaching apart as a surgeon takes a field apart — hand to the record before eyes to the person, eyes before mouth, the half-beat in the gap — and files it as her ninth record-first hand on a place of its own with a finger between it and Hessa Rale's eighth; he files no tenth, makes no reader of her keeping, joins her to none and makes no figure of the slate's nearness. **T080 advanced and NOT paid:** she is expressly not the speaker of any voice that came over the boards — the Frost 14 well-saying stays at one saying and four shapings with no fifth, the burned-slate word at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with no witness — and no ownerless voice came over the boards on Stone 28 or this morning. The carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and eighty-eight days (T088). Answer **351** filed on the towel in the small hours, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, laid across neither the eleven readings, the bell's gap, the flat knock, the covered grain, the handful, the thumb's resting, the held breath, the two bites of iron, the river's skin, the widow's mark, the fourth direction nor the keeping at the fold.

scenes.title: The Day Before the Last
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, no new dated heading: the afternoon of Stone 29 through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day with answer 352. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge and damper; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons only: a Cold Acre hare-carrier, a cracked-jar man in a rope sling, a woman with a basket of kindling, two fence-menders. No Ilva, Berr, Hessa, collector, green-mouthed woman or foundling; no market, Cross or bell; no ownerless voice — the four directions stand where put and do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). Dramatic purpose: let every held thing gather interest without being paid, and hold the afternoon still on the day before the year's last reading. The afternoon comes down thin through the finger's-width door and goes on without a boundary drawn; the yard goes around its seven places with a look and a wide step and no number, once and not twice (T009/T013/T092). The hare-carrier's price is answered with the weather, the cracked-jar man is sent to a pot that says nothing, and to the woman with kindling asking what the seventh year will want and the fence-menders wanting the thaw early and late Tarn says Yes, house to each and keeps the late because it puts off the paying (T077). Six pieces stand in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, the small knife at the very edge of its sill; his hand passes over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, the coming away the whole of the checking, and he tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count. The Ash 14 held breath and the Bone 26 thumb's resting are found where put and not made again; he brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year now at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist catching and giving back the little light, his stroke over the bright flagstones without the half-check (T036/T076/T006). Jorra's meal-fine grey dust is ground small as meal past the bent little finger and white in a fist-crease; men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey and get no name from him; dusty forearms are parted from clean as clot from vessel; the wheel and a pot are spoken to before any person; the bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence and comes out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time (T062/T035/T031). The burned slate stands at five with a finger between the fifth and the four, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with no sixth and no witness, the well-saying at four shapings with no fifth; the nine record-first hands keep no tenth and the nine stoppings keep no tenth. At the going of the light Sella carries him up and never into the Debt Loft, sets him on his bed, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and adds no second fold, tells the coals it is the thaw, says the house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, turns the dressed grain under wool with no figure and no handful and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat; the widow's mark hangs untouched because a going of the light and a bed are not openings and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule with no eighth made due (T058/T079/T100, T077). In the small hours the file comes out and every gap is left a gap: six hearings beside and never among with the seventh place empty and the Drawing's knock outside; the heard bell in its square beside the told, four, four and a gap, kept in its square and not folded into any count; three counts in three places not becoming one; four rooms with the same gap held apart; the five held objects with the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath and the damper holding beside them, each on its own place with a finger between; eleven arithmetics behind one unsigned figure with the twelfth standing one morning off, unbrought and not earned by this day. Answer **352** filed exact, complete and worth nothing, the surgeon's small clean satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found costing nothing, which is how he knows it is not peace.

scenes.title: The Twelfth Arithmetic
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry and the third dated \daymark{389}{Stone 30, Tenthday, Y.H. 813}: the year's third and last Account-day and market, from before first light to the going of the light, with answer 353. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T015/T041/T047):** the twelfth arithmetic of the year goes up behind one unsigned figure — the three of Frost, the first, second and third of Bone, the first, second and third of Ash, and Stone's first, second and last — and twelve are twelve and not one account, the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space between and no doctrine comes out of twelve. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Berr Clay and Hessa Rale; Garl Vail in objects only. Walk-ons only: the two hundred at the Cross, eight pigs driven over the wet reading block, a man with a number in his fist sent to a slate at the watch, the soft-cuffed clerk at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, a silent woman with the sweetish green of lead glaze at one corner of her mouth at the pot board, and a small shape in cast-offs at the market's edge. No Ilva, Tarn, Jorra, Drawing collector, green coat or named officer; no ownerless voice over the boards — the four directions stand where put and do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). New day, new date, no recap: nothing from Stone 28 or 29 crosses under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Dramatic purpose: the district's arithmetic changes for the twelfth time in the year and cannot be changed back, while the boy refuses to let twelve likenesses stand up and call themselves an account, for an account wants a hand to lay them together and a payer under all twelve and no such hand or payer stands. The surgeon takes the body in its old order and knows a basket set level out of the draught where the heat comes sideways is the careful rewarming he would choose and cannot ask for, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from the outside and slowly, while the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrels without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086). Sella carries him down the nineteen steps before first light at the half-pace from every open slate, gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off through the reading and the bell, giving no instruction and no reason to the basket (T058/T079). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road to the reading block under the moot-post with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay of him the smell of nothing at all; his large clean hands wipe the thumb twice before touching nothing, once for the slate and once for the figure that will be on it, hold a narrow slate unopened against the forearm with the writing inward, pass a finger over the figure through the cloth of his own sleeve and let his eyes rest on the writing a breath longer than the writing required. He reads One in twelve, as the notice says low into the goers-by and sends the figure twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that come late, never looking into it. He calls the levy and denies it with The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon draws a hand from a field before the dressing goes on; to the man with the number in his fist he sends a slate at the watch, and something low he says to the block about kindness being entered, in the tone of a man setting a cup where a cup belongs, and the block answers nothing. He goes off up the clay road toward High Kiln with the cord folded, the narrow slate under his arm and the box locked, Stone's last true subtraction riding inside beside the eleven that went before, believing he has done a kindness, with no anger in him and no triumph — the belief that will one day be remembered against him. The twelve true subtractions ride locked in his box, the key gone up in a coat pocket that does not come back down and the boy has no key (T015/T041/T047). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told bell of the Long Night and its gap not folded into any count and not made a seventh (T078). Hessa Rale goes up the clay road toward Greybank before noon with the narrow slate held edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned to her sleeve, the thumb along the grain of the frame and nothing pressing where the writing is, hand to slate before eyes to crowd, giving no figure, not made a reader by the year's last figure and joined to none; her eighth record-first hand stays eight with no tenth (T080 held). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and slate to his forearm, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market selling over him as water goes over a stone (T090 held). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman's sweetish green stays a colour and at the market's edge a small shape in cast-offs stays a shape, with no eighth of either, neither named, joined, given a loaf, a slate or a sale, and never Fenna or Ulda in the narration (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The dressed grain covered under wool at home is read over by a figure that does not know what it cost (T077). Sella carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what has been read over the wicker. In the small hours the file comes out on the towel with every gap left gap; he files twelve arithmetics on a place of their own with a finger between them and the eleven readings' finding, the keeping, the four rooms' gap and the four directions, and refuses to make a row come out even. Answer **353** filed exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer.

scenes.title: The Year Goes Out Without a Boundary
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: the end of Stone 30 at the going of the light and in the small hours, with answer 354 and the count at 389 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail; Garl Vail in objects. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, Tarn, Jorra, collector, runner, market, Cross or bell after the carry home; no ownerless voice over the boards — the Ash 5 joining and the Ash 17, Ash 23 and Stone 23 directions stand where put, do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 held). Dramatic purpose: check every object and leave every gap a gap, let the twelve readings, the keeping and the four directions gather interest without being paid, and close on forward motion toward the Five. At the going of the light Sella sets him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and adds no second fold; the thread stays frozen and unwiped; the wool stays found where put and is not made again, still a finding and not a placing, with no second fold, third crust, name, gift, payment or payer, and the far-off finger that would lay shelf and fold together and call the joining an account is still far off, not his, not come (T097/T060/T086 held). She goes to the hearth before the basket, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says the house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row and figures neither gap, glances once at the clay jar standing cold under lead glaze with the sweetish edge coming and going on a wrong wind past the pot board and shuts her hand half over nothing, the little-door burn on the back of her left hand closing on air. The widow's mark at her throat, the cord oiled where a working thumb has touched it ten thousand times, is not touched: a market, a going of the light and a bed are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule, and no eighth was made due. On the pot board the twice-mended pot is lifted thumb-first where the wire crosses the crack before the weight comes on the handle, so that the hairline of the original break shows between the old-brass staple and the tighter wire; Leave the crack showing. People trust a thing they can see has been handled and If it's worth mending it's worth mending twice. The second time is the real one go to the pot and the fire and never to a person, improved in the keeping and very likely not as good as Garl said them; repair stays apart from restoration. The dressed grain is turned once under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child, lifting no figure and taking no handful. The pot rim is set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; inside the wool his hand goes toward the rim and stops where the half-beat stopped it, the interval bought at nothing and not a gift and the stopping his. Under the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and eighty-nine days (T088). In the small hours the towel comes out as instruments come out when a case is done and before the next is called, with every gap left gap. Twelve arithmetics of the year — the three of Frost, the first, second and third of Bone, the first, second and third of Ash and Stone's first, second and last — stand behind one unsigned figure: one in twelve, read twice over the basket on Stone 30 and sent twice, once for the moot and once for the late households. The figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space between, twelve are twelve and not one account and no doctrine stands up out of twelve; the twelve true subtractions ride locked in Berr Clay's box up the clay road, the key gone up in a coat pocket that does not come back down and the boy having no key. Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among, the sixth the small flat knock out of Dessa Silt as the men lifted her, the seventh place empty and not dug for; the Drawing's flat knock stays outside them on its own place; the heard bell stays in its square beside the told, four, four and a gap; the four rooms with the same gap are held apart with a finger between every pair; nine record-first hands and nine stoppings keep no tenth; the burned-slate word stands at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with no witness and the well-saying at four shapings; the five held objects stand with the pot-crack resting, the hand-at-the-sill breath and the damper holding beside them, each with a finger between, and the keeping beside them and expressly not a tenth. No sixth hearing, seventh opening, tenth hand, tenth stopping, eighth opening, thirteenth arithmetic, witness, reader or payment was supplied to make a row come out even, for a finding filled to make a row come out even is a finding forged. Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water under the winter skin, a covering put on by the cold and taken off by the cold and entered nowhere, found where put and not made again, not spent on the reading or on the going of the light and not made to buy a lesson (T083/T085 held). The hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the note, does not reach, takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing under the covering, lets it go as the note ended and comes straight down and lays itself flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking; the note had done before the hand came down, so the letting-go was neither early nor stayed, and the hand did not stay. He files answer **354**: exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across neither the twelve readings, the bell's gap, the flat knock, the child's grey fingertips, the mother's cup, the covered grain, the handful, the thumb's resting, the held breath, the two bites of iron, the river's skin, the widow's mark, the fourth direction nor the keeping at the fold. Stone keeps its twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth and thirtieth days without a boundary drawn, the deep-winter month holding both its names — older women by weather, slatemen by Grathic Account-days — neither set right nor left in so many words; the year ends without a boundary drawn and the Five stand beyond, unbrought. The count stands at **three hundred and eighty-nine exact**, six months and two hundred and nine days told by nobody who would have known what a number counted, the carried fire's fifth unpaid the same number and its payer unnamed, and Garl's name unspoken the same number. The surgeon's small clean satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found costs nothing, which is how he knows it is not peace; under it, louder, the infant wants the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, and gets none of the three, both true, the second louder, neither winning, no verdict in the quarrel and none looked for. Twelve findings are twelve findings and not a rule; twelve arithmetics are twelve and not one account; four directions are four and not a witness. The hand lies flat on the fold on answer three hundred and fifty-four, the crust's corner standing a hair off the wool, and the count goes on under the roof in Low Kiln, Sill, Grath.
